science: Why astronauts float: the station is always falling around the Earth, and everything inside falls with it.
Earth looks blue from space because most of it is covered with water; the white swirls are clouds.
Handrails and Velcro keep astronauts and their things from floating away.
Astronauts eat tortillas instead of bread, so there are no floating crumbs.
parent.summary: A shy new helper robot arrives on a supply ship. The crew says hello, shows Button around, and throws a welcome party.

options: Wave: Button waves back so hard it somersaults.
Sing: a hello song makes Button's tummy light glow.

paths.moment: Race to the window, or show Button the way
options: Race: Button is left behind and its light goes dim. The crew notices, comes back, says sorry, and brings Button along.
Show the way: they float down the station hand in hand.
Sunny yellow or ocean blue. Either one, Tommy lights it up.

talk: How do you think Button felt when it was new and didn't know anybody?
What can you do to help someone who is new feel welcome?
Why does everything float on the space station?

beats.say: High above the Earth, a little space station sails around and around.
Its name is Star Station.
Star Station has a very special crew: {crew}!
But this morning, the station is still asleep. {T}, can you wake it up? Tap, tap, tap!
Good morning, Star Station!
Inside the station, everything floats.
{a}'s hair floats up, up, up.
And look! {t}'s sock is floating away. Wheee!
{T}, can you catch the sock? Tap it!
Got it! What a catch!
Why does everything float up here?
Here's the secret. Our whole station is always falling around the Earth. Swooping around and around, and never landing.
And everything inside swoops right along with it. So everything floats!
That's why there are handrails to hold on to, and Velcro to keep things from floating away.
{a} stuck the sock on a Velcro patch. Rrrip... stick!
Bing, bong! A little supply ship had docked with the station.
It brought food, and water, and... something else.
The round hatch swung open. Inside were boxes and boxes, floating in a jumble.
Then, peek! Two glowing eyes looked out from behind a box.
And zip! They hid again.
It was a little round robot. A brand-new helper for Star Station.
But the robot was shy.

choice.say: {A}, how should we say hello to our new friend?

beats.say: {crew} waved a big, slow, friendly wave.
The little robot peeked out. It waved back, with both arms...
...so hard that it spun around in a slow, floaty somersault.
"Whoops-a-daisy," beeped the robot. "Hello!"
{crew} sang a hello song, soft and sweet.
Hello, hello, we're glad you came! Hello, new friend. What is your name?
The little robot floated out, slow and careful.
A round button on its tummy began to glow, warm and orange.
"My name is Button," said the robot. "Because of this!"
Button pressed the round button on its tummy. Boop!
{T}, can you help Button boop? Tap anywhere!
Button giggled a beepy giggle. Beep, boo, hee hee!
"I'm new here," said Button. "Everything is so big. And so... floaty."
Just then, the big window at the end of the station began to glow, blue and bright.
The Earth was coming into view! It's the best view on the whole station.
{crew} wanted to see it right away.

options.label: Zoom!
options.say: Zoom to the window, right now?

beats.say: Zoom! Whoosh! {crew} raced off toward the window.
But wait. Where was Button?
Button was still back by the boxes, all alone. Its tummy light had gone dim.
Button didn't know the way. Everything was so new.
{crew} looked back, and saw Button there, all by itself.
[So they|So {a}] zoomed all the way back.
"Sorry, Button! [We|I] didn't mean to leave you behind. Come with [us|me]!"
[They held out their hands.|{a} held out a hand.] And Button's tummy light glowed bright again.
"Come with [us|me], Button!" said {a}. "[We'll|I'll] show you the way."
[{a} took one of Button's hands, and {t} took the other.|{a} took Button's little hand.]
Together, they floated down the station. Past the handrails. Past the Velcro patches.
And Button's tummy light glowed brighter, and brighter.
And there it was. The Cupola! A round room made of windows.
Seven windows, looking out at the Earth, and the stars.
"Ooooooh," said Button.
The Earth was so big, and so blue.
Most of the Earth is covered with water. That's why it looks so blue!
And those white swirls? Those are clouds.
Our station zooms around the Earth super, super fast. There's always something new to see.
{T}, can you wave hello to the Earth? Tap anywhere!
Hello, Earth!
"Let's have a welcome party for Button!" said {a}.
Star Station's party lights can glow in any color you like.

choice.say: {A}, what color should we make the lights for Button's party?

beats.say: What a great color! Now, {T}, can you light up the station? Tap, tap, tap!
The whole station glowed sunny yellow, like the inside of a lemon drop.
The whole station glowed ocean blue, like the inside of a wave.
Then came the party snacks.
In space, we usually eat tortillas instead of bread. Bread makes crumbs, and crumbs float everywhere!
A tortilla drifted by, like a little flying saucer.
{t} took a big bite. Munch, munch, munch.
Button didn't eat anything. Robots don't. But Button did a happy little dance, spinning slowly in the air.
"Thank you for saying hello," said Button. "I don't feel shy anymore."
"Welcome aboard, Button," said {crew}.
Below them, the Earth turned slowly. Blue, and white, and beautiful.
And Star Station sailed on, around and around, with its whole crew together.
